summary: A target-level continuation of the three inherited GC.2 targets. It imports the reviewed full function-field idele nodes, retains the actual noninjective modified-unit action, identifies the signed right quotient with generically trivialized root lines and proves the separate Picard quotient by explicit labelled Hom descent. Its degree uses O_X(−E), and its stabilizers retain root signs and the locally-square constant extension. One precise completed-divisor-lattice supplier contract remains; no new ordinary Picard, restricted-product or curve theory is planned here.

nodes.title: The modified-unit kernel and residue-square quotient
nodes.statement: The projection H→U has kernel canonically ∏_{x∈R} μ₂(κ_x), via the retained root coordinates, and image U_sq={u∈U : ū_x is a square in κ_x× for every x∈R}. Reduction followed by residue square class induces U/p(H) ≅ ∏_{x∈R} κ_x×/(κ_x×)². Thus 1→∏ μ₂(κ_x)→H→U→∏ κ_x×/(κ_x×)²→1 is exact as a sequence of abelian groups. The last arrow is onto. At R=∅ its last two nontrivial terms identify H with U. No fibre-product ring is required.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, F=k(X), and R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, possibly empty.

Places are all closed points of X, including the points outside an affine chart. F_x is the normalized completed valuation field, O_x its valuation ring, and κ_x its residue field. The curve/place and residue identifications use the named suppliers.
I=∏′_x F_x× relative to O_x×; U=∏_x O_x×; H=O_{√R}× is the inherited modified-unit group. Write p:H→I for its actual homomorphism. Set E(a)=Σ_x ord_x(a_x)[x], with ord_x(π_x)=1.
All groupoids retain labelled morphisms. A right arrow h:a→b means b=a p(h); a double arrow (f,h):a→b means b=diag(f) a p(h). Local root-unit coordinates satisfy ū_x=v_x².
proofSteps: Apply the native valuation-subring residue-unit surjection at each branch point. The curve/completion residue comparison is part of FA.2/projective-adeles and its AlgebraicCurves Layer 5 prerequisite.
An element of the projection kernel has u=1 and v_x²=1. Conversely these labels produce every kernel element, without identifying different labels.

A unit tuple lifts exactly when all branch residues have square roots. Reduction onto the finitely many branch residue-unit groups is onto; the product of their square-class quotients is therefore the cokernel.
acceptance: For a branch point in odd characteristic, the coordinate (1,−1) is a nonidentity kernel label.
A residue nonsquare is excluded from p(H), even though it belongs to U.
The product is over closed branch points: |ker p|=2^{#|R|}, not 2^{deg R}.

sources.locator: A.1.6, pp. 517–518; Lemma A.5 proof, p. 518
sources.match: The source supplies the residue-square fibre products and their frame-changing action. The exact kernel/image/cokernel sequence is an explicit algebraic deduction from those definitions, not a separately numbered claim of the paper.

nodes.title: Root lines with a generic trivialization
nodes.statement: Let G_R(X) be the groupoid of (L,K_R,ι,τ_η), where (L,K_R,ι) is the inherited k-point of Pic_X^√R and τ_η:L|Spec F≅F is an F-linear trivialization. An arrow (φ,ψ) satisfies φ|R∘ι=ι′∘ψ^{⊗2} and τ′_η∘φ_η=τ_η. Tensor product multiplies generic trivializations, the unit has its standard generic trivialization, and duality inverts it. Forgetting τ_η maps to the existing root Picard groupoid. Degree is deg L and may have either sign.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, F=k(X), and R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, possibly empty.

Places are all closed points of X, including the points outside an affine chart. F_x is the normalized completed valuation field, O_x its valuation ring, and κ_x its residue field. The curve/place and residue identifications use the named suppliers.
I=∏′_x F_x× relative to O_x×; U=∏_x O_x×; H=O_{√R}× is the inherited modified-unit group. Write p:H→I for its actual homomorphism. Set E(a)=Σ_x ord_x(a_x)[x], with ord_x(π_x)=1.
All groupoids retain labelled morphisms. A right arrow h:a→b means b=a p(h); a double arrow (f,h):a→b means b=diag(f) a p(h). Local root-unit coordinates satisfy ū_x=v_x².
proofSteps: Add only a generic trivialization to the existing root-line triple; use its existing line-bundle isomorphisms, tensor product and duality.
Restrict arrows to those preserving the generic frame. The square-root diagram remains part of each arrow, so root automorphisms are retained.
Tensor, dual, restriction and their coherence are imported from GC.0 and the ordinary Picard-groupoid supplier.
acceptance: The forgetful functor remembers the entire root-line triple and forgets exactly the generic frame.
No section or effectivity condition is added; G_R is defined in all realized degrees.

sources.match: The fully framed source proof separates the generic frame from the local/root frames. Retaining the former after forgetting the latter gives this intermediate groupoid; it supplies the right quotient used in §6.2.3.

uses.how: Identifies the geometric object represented by the signed right quotient without discarding the generic frame.
Makes O_X(−E) and its branch root intrinsic before the further Picard quotient.

api.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.mk
api.statement: Build an object from a root-line triple and an actual generic-fibre isomorphism.

api.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.forget
api.statement: Forget the generic trivialization to Pic_X^√R(k), on both objects and arrows.

api.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.hom_ext
api.statement: Two arrows are equal exactly when their line-bundle and root-line isomorphisms agree; a root label is never inferred from the line isomorphism alone.

api.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.hom_iff
api.statement: A pair of isomorphisms is an arrow exactly when it respects both the root square diagram and the displayed generic-frame equality.

api.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.tensor
api.statement: Tensor the line bundles, roots, square identifications and generic frames; associators, unitors and symmetry are inherited coherently.

api.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.dual
api.statement: Dualize all data and invert the generic trivialization, with the usual evaluation isomorphisms to the unit.

api.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.degree
api.statement: Return deg L; this is invariant under arrows, additive under tensor product and negated by duality.

api.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.changeGenericFrame
api.statement: For f∈F× multiply τ_η by f. This is an F× action with identity and composition laws; forgetting the frame is invariant under it.

tests.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.test_empty_R
tests.statement: For R=∅, forgetting root data identifies G_∅ with ordinary generically trivialized line bundles; through the ordinary divisor dictionary it is equivalent to the discrete groupoid of signed divisors.

tests.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.test_generic_frame_matters
tests.statement: For f∈F× with nonzero principal divisor, the trivial root line at R=∅ with generic frames 1 and f gives nonisomorphic objects of G_∅, although forgetting the generic frame gives the same line bundle.

tests.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.test_root_squareclass
tests.statement: On X=P¹ over F₅ with R={0}, take L=O_X, K_R=F₅ and τ_η=1. The square identifications with coefficients 1 and 2 give nonisomorphic objects of G_R, both of valuation divisor 0.

tests.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.GenericFramedRootLine.test_dual
tests.statement: For every A, A⊗A^∨ is isomorphic to the unit with its standard generic frame; its degree is 0, even when A has negative degree.

nodes.title: The fully framed root Picard groupoid
nodes.statement: Let F_R(X) have objects (L,K_R,ι,τ_η,(τ_x)_x,(t_x)_{x∈R}), extending G_R(X). Each τ_x is an O_x-linear isomorphism L⊗O_x≅O_x; each t_x is a κ_x-linear isomorphism K_x≅κ_x, and (τ_x mod m_x)∘ι_x=t_x^{⊗2}. Morphisms preserve the root triple and every frame. The transition coefficient is a_x=τ_η∘τ_x^{-1} after extension to F_x. There is no extra summability axiom: for an algebraic line bundle and a rational frame these coefficients are units at all but finitely many x. The forgetful functor to G_R forgets τ_x and t_x. Tensor and dual are componentwise.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, F=k(X), and R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, possibly empty.

Places are all closed points of X, including the points outside an affine chart. F_x is the normalized completed valuation field, O_x its valuation ring, and κ_x its residue field. The curve/place and residue identifications use the named suppliers.
I=∏′_x F_x× relative to O_x×; U=∏_x O_x×; H=O_{√R}× is the inherited modified-unit group. Write p:H→I for its actual homomorphism. Set E(a)=Σ_x ord_x(a_x)[x], with ord_x(π_x)=1.
All groupoids retain labelled morphisms. A right arrow h:a→b means b=a p(h); a double arrow (f,h):a→b means b=diag(f) a p(h). Local root-unit coordinates satisfy ū_x=v_x².
proofSteps: Use the ordinary curve/divisor dictionary and local freeness to obtain the generic and completed local frames; root fibres are one-dimensional over their residue fields.
Forgetting a compatible root frame and its root line over a fixed ordinary frame has contractible fibre: the framed residue line with square identification is uniquely isomorphic to the standard one.

The requested completed-lattice dictionary proves that local transition coefficients are integral units away from a finite divisor; use the reciprocal of the source proof’s printed transition ratio, as recorded in EGC2-1.
Frame-preserving arrows and tensor coherence are inherited; a line map fixed on the generic fibre is determined everywhere on the integral curve.
acceptance: All its automorphism groups are trivial, including the root-line automorphisms, because the root frames must also be preserved.
Its local-frame compatibility is an equation of isomorphisms of lines, not a choice of square root of a transition scalar in F_x.

sources.locator: Lemma A.5, complete proof and frame diagram, p. 518
sources.match: The source uses generic, completed local and residue-root frames to parametrize ideles. This node makes its morphisms and frame equation explicit. The transition ratio is corrected to match the source’s inverse-uniformizer normalization and §6.2.3.

uses.how: Provides the discrete idele presentation before forgetting frames.
Makes local/root and generic frame changes independent, with their full labels.

api.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.FullyFramedRootLine.mk
api.statement: Construct the fully framed object from the root-line triple, generic frame, local frames and compatible root frames.

api.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.FullyFramedRootLine.forgetLocalFrames
api.statement: Forget all local and root frames to G_R; preserve τ_η.

api.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.FullyFramedRootLine.forgetRootFrames
api.statement: Forget K_R,ι,t_x to the ordinary fully framed Picard groupoid; the functor is an equivalence.

api.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.FullyFramedRootLine.coefficient
api.statement: The coefficient at x is the scalar τ_η∘τ_x^{-1}; it is a unit of F_x, and these coefficients form an idele.

api.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.FullyFramedRootLine.hom_ext
api.statement: A fully frame-preserving isomorphism is unique when it exists; both the ordinary line and the root line maps are fixed by their frames.

api.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.FullyFramedRootLine.changeFrames
api.statement: For (f,h) with h=(u,v), change τ_η to fτ_η, τ_x to u_x^{-1}τ_x and t_x to v_x^{-1}t_x. The root frame equation is preserved, and the coefficient changes to diag(f) a p(h). This is an action functorial on arrows, with identity and composition laws; forgetLocalFrames intertwines it with changeGenericFrame.

api.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.FullyFramedRootLine.tensor
api.statement: Multiply the coefficients under tensor product; unit coefficients are 1 and dual coefficients are inverse. The inherited associator, unitor and symmetry maps preserve all frames.

tests.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.FullyFramedRootLine.test_empty_R
tests.statement: For R=∅ this is the ordinary fully framed Picard groupoid; its coefficient functor identifies it with the discrete groupoid on the full idele group, including the infinity factors.

tests.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.FullyFramedRootLine.test_uniformizer_inverse
tests.statement: For x∉R the line O_X(x), its standard generic frame and the local frame π_x·(−) at x has coefficient π_x^{-1}; all other local frames can be chosen with coefficient 1.

tests.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.FullyFramedRootLine.test_root_sign_contractible
tests.statement: Replace one root frame t_x by −t_x while keeping the ordinary data. The two fully framed tuples are uniquely isomorphic by root-line scalar −1 at x; this does not create another idele coefficient or an automorphism.

tests.name: TauCeti.RamifiedClassField.FullyFramedRootLine.test_no_unframed_kernel
tests.statement: A nontrivial root-line sign cannot be an automorphism preserving the chosen t_x. The nontrivial root signs become automorphisms only after the local/root frames are forgotten.

nodes.title: Idele gluing with the sign fixed by local lattices
nodes.statement: The coefficient functor F_R(X)→Discrete(I), A↦(τ_η∘τ_x^{-1})_x, is an equivalence. Its inverse sends a to the line L(a)=O_X(−E(a)) as a subsheaf of the constant rational line F, whose completed lattice is a_xO_x, together with τ_η the rational identity, τ_x division by a_x, K_R=O_R, t_x=1 and ι_x sending 1 to the residue of the completed basis a_x. This is a symmetric monoidal equivalence for tensor product versus idele multiplication. Its coefficient equations commute with the F××H frame changes specified above.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, F=k(X), and R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, possibly empty.

Places are all closed points of X, including the points outside an affine chart. F_x is the normalized completed valuation field, O_x its valuation ring, and κ_x its residue field. The curve/place and residue identifications use the named suppliers.
I=∏′_x F_x× relative to O_x×; U=∏_x O_x×; H=O_{√R}× is the inherited modified-unit group. Write p:H→I for its actual homomorphism. Set E(a)=Σ_x ord_x(a_x)[x], with ord_x(π_x)=1.
All groupoids retain labelled morphisms. A right arrow h:a→b means b=a p(h); a double arrow (f,h):a→b means b=diag(f) a p(h). Local root-unit coordinates satisfy ū_x=v_x².
proofSteps: Use finite support of E(a) and the ordinary divisor sheaf O_X(−E(a)); its completed-lattice identification is the precise AC.12 supplier request.
The local element a_x is a basis of this completed rank-one lattice. Its residue basis defines ι_x for the trivial root line, giving a fully framed object with coefficient a.

For an arbitrary framed line, its generic embedding identifies every completed lattice with a_xO_x. The ordinary dictionary identifies the algebraic line with O_X(−E(a)); the frame diagram uniquely identifies the residue-root data.
A framed arrow exists exactly when the coefficients agree and is then unique. Multiplication, identity and inversion of bases give the monoidal comparison and frame-change equivariance.
acceptance: The coefficient π_x maps to O_X(−x), and π_x^{-1} maps to O_X(x).
The construction needs no rational point or degree-one divisor and makes no claim that a global element has the prescribed local coefficients.
The inverse is specified by divisor sheaves, rather than an unspecified general formal-patching theorem.

sources.match: Lemma A.5 uses the fully framed idele comparison. The lattice construction spells out its ordinary gluing input and fixes its frame-ratio misprint consistently with the lemma statement and the signed divisor use.

nodes.title: The signed right quotient represents generically framed root lines
nodes.statement: The inherited right-action groupoid Div^√R(X)=I//H is symmetrically monoidally equivalent to G_R(X). The functor sends a to (L(a),K_R(a),ι(a),τ_η). A labelled arrow h=(u,v):a→b=a p(h) acts by the identity on the rational line and by v_x^{-1} on the standard root lines. Under this equivalence E:I//H→Discrete(Div(X)) is the negative of the divisor of the rational section sent to 1 by τ_η; the line is O_X(−E). The induced functor Q to the inherited double-action presentation sends a to a and h to (1,h). The geometric square with G_R(X)→Pic_X^√R(k) commutes up to a specified monoidal natural isomorphism.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, F=k(X), and R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, possibly empty.

Places are all closed points of X, including the points outside an affine chart. F_x is the normalized completed valuation field, O_x its valuation ring, and κ_x its residue field. The curve/place and residue identifications use the named suppliers.
I=∏′_x F_x× relative to O_x×; U=∏_x O_x×; H=O_{√R}× is the inherited modified-unit group. Write p:H→I for its actual homomorphism. Set E(a)=Σ_x ord_x(a_x)[x], with ord_x(π_x)=1.
All groupoids retain labelled morphisms. A right arrow h:a→b means b=a p(h); a double arrow (f,h):a→b means b=diag(f) a p(h). Local root-unit coordinates satisfy ū_x=v_x².
proofSteps: Apply the fully framed comparison, then forget local and residue-root frames while keeping the generic frame.
Two sets of compatible local frames differ by a unique h∈H. Their root-coordinate difference, even in ker p, is a distinct arrow after forgetting the frames.
For b=a u the line lattices agree. The line identity and root scalar v^{-1} respect ι since ū=v². Conversely every generic-frame-preserving root-line arrow has exactly this label.
Forgetting the remaining generic frame is the double-quotient inclusion h↦(1,h); the same frame maps give the natural square and its tensor coherence.
acceptance: For R=∅ this reduces to the discrete groupoid of signed divisors, rather than their divisor classes.
A nonconstant principal idele with nonzero divisor is distinct from the unit in the right quotient.
The map on root-line fibres is v^{-1}, a sign convention checked against the root square diagram; p is not replaced by its image subgroup.

sources.match: The right quotient and its further Picard map are explicitly used in §6.2.3. The intermediate generic-frame equivalence and commuting square are extracted from the separate frame changes in A.5, with the morphisms written out.

nodes.title: Full morphism descent for the Picard double quotient
nodes.statement: For a,b∈I, gluing gives a bijection {(f,h)∈F××H : b=diag(f)a p(h)} ≅ Isom_{Pic_X^√R(k)}(L(a)^♮,L(b)^♮). If h=(u,v), the line map is multiplication by f on the rational line and the root map is multiplication by v_x^{-1}. These bijections preserve identity, composition, tensor product and inverse. Every root-line triple admits generic and compatible local/root frames, so they give the inherited Lemma A.5 equivalence with full faithfulness and essential surjectivity. Q:I//H→I//(F××H) is faithful, with arrow label h↦(1,h), and is the functor that forgets the generic frame.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, F=k(X), and R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, possibly empty.

Places are all closed points of X, including the points outside an affine chart. F_x is the normalized completed valuation field, O_x its valuation ring, and κ_x its residue field. The curve/place and residue identifications use the named suppliers.
I=∏′_x F_x× relative to O_x×; U=∏_x O_x×; H=O_{√R}× is the inherited modified-unit group. Write p:H→I for its actual homomorphism. Set E(a)=Σ_x ord_x(a_x)[x], with ord_x(π_x)=1.
All groupoids retain labelled morphisms. A right arrow h:a→b means b=a p(h); a double arrow (f,h):a→b means b=diag(f) a p(h). Local root-unit coordinates satisfy ū_x=v_x².
proofSteps: An isomorphism of line bundles on the integral curve is multiplication by a unique f on their generic embeddings. Comparing completed lattices gives u_x=b_x/(f a_x)∈O_x× at every x.
Write the root-line map as a scalar ψ_x. The root square diagram says ψ_x²=overline(f a_x/b_x)=ū_x^{-1}; set v_x=ψ_x^{-1}. Thus (u,v)∈H. This recovers every label uniquely.

Conversely these equations ensure that multiplication by f carries each completed lattice to the other and the root squares commute. The completed-lattice dictionary used in the preceding comparison supplies the actual algebraic line map.

Generic fibres and residue-root fibres are one-dimensional. Choose frames and lift the needed residue-unit adjustments to completed local frames using the residue-unit surjection; this proves essential surjectivity.
Products of labels give compositions and tensors because the groups are abelian. The embedding h↦(1,h) is injective, proving faithfulness of Q, without claiming it is full.
acceptance: For R=∅ every Picard automorphism is a scalar in k×, so the result cannot be replaced by a bijection of class groups.
The arrow (f,1) connects a and diag(f)a in the double presentation, even when no such right-quotient arrow exists.
Root signs survive as distinct arrows with the same ordinary line map.

sources.locator: Lemma A.5, (A.4) and proof, p. 518; §6.2.3, p. 498
sources.match: A.5 identifies the full double quotient with the root Picard groupoid. This node supplies the explicit Hom bijections, their coherence and the further-quotient functor that the source uses implicitly; it is a refinement of the inherited node, not a second definition.

nodes.title: Signed divisor fibres with their square classes and stabilizers
nodes.statement: For each signed divisor D of X, the fibre of E:I//H→Discrete(Div(X)) is nonempty. Its isomorphism classes form a torsor under U/p(H)≅∏_{x∈R}κ_x×/(κ_x×)². Every object has automorphism group canonically ker p≅∏_{x∈R}μ₂(κ_x), using its arrow labels. Choosing an idele with E(a)=D and representatives of the square classes yields an equivalence with the disjoint union, indexed by that square-class product, of the classifying groupoid of ∏μ₂(κ_x). This last presentation depends on the choices; the torsor action and the labelled stabilizer identification do not. For r=#|R| there are 2^r components, each with automorphism group of order 2^r.

proofSteps: Surjectivity of the imported idele divisor map gives a base object in the fibre; all other objects differ by an integral unit tuple.
The right-unit quotient of that unit tuple is U/p(H), whose square-class description is the preceding exact sequence.
Use the native action-category stabilizer/endomorphism identification. Translation on I gives stabilizer exactly ker p, retaining every label.

A transitive group action component is equivalent to the classifying groupoid of a stabilizer after choosing an object and connecting arrows. Finite odd residue fields have two square classes and two square roots of 1.

For X=P¹/F₃ and R a single degree-two closed point, each divisor fibre has two components and each stabilizer has order two. The count is not four.
A product of classifying groupoids alone would miss the square-class components over the finite base field.

nodes.title: The stabilizer extension in the double quotient
nodes.statement: For every idele a, its automorphism group in the double-action presentation is canonically A_R={(c,(v_x)) : c∈k×, v_x∈κ_x×, v_x²=c^{-1} for every x∈R}, under componentwise multiplication. Let C_R={c∈k× : c is a square in every κ_x×}. Projection gives an exact sequence 1→∏_{x∈R}μ₂(κ_x)→A_R→C_R→1. This sequence is not asserted to split. For finite odd k, C_R=(k×)² if R has an odd-degree closed point, and C_R=k× if every closed branch point has even degree; the latter includes R=∅. At R=∅, A_R=k×.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, F=k(X), and R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, possibly empty.

proofSteps: At a fixed idele a a double automorphism satisfies diag(f)p(h)=1. The ordinary line automorphism is a global unit, hence f=c∈k× by the ordinary proper-curve Picard supplier.
Then u_x=c^{-1} at every place, and the remaining labelled equations are v_x²=c^{-1}. This gives A_R and the exact projection sequence.
For κ_x/k of degree d and q=|k|, a nonsquare constant stays nonsquare exactly when d is odd: the exponent (q^d−1)/(q−1) has parity d. Apply the finite-field square criterion.
The kernel is the same labelled root-sign group, but its quotient is only the constants locally square at all branch points. Check the nonsplit example rather than choosing an unjustified section.
acceptance: For X=P¹/F₅ and R={0}, v↦(v^{-2},v) identifies A_R with F₅×≅C₄. The element (c=4,v=2) has order four, while the proposed split C₂×C₂ has none.
With two rational branch points over F₃, A_R has order four and retains two independent root signs.
For X=P¹/F₃ and one degree-two branch point, C_R=F₃×; the nontrivial constant lifts only after using a square root in F₉.

nodes.title: The valuation divisor and Picard degree have opposite signs
nodes.statement: Let Φ:I//(F××H)≃Pic_X^√R(k) be the inherited equivalence with the corrected frame-ratio convention. For a∈I, the ordinary line of Φ(a) is O_X(−E(a)) and deg Φ(a)=−deg E(a)=−Σ_x ord_x(a_x)[κ_x:k]. The same formula holds for Q(a) from the right quotient, is invariant under every labelled double arrow, and defines its integer grading. Tensor product adds this grading; duality negates it. After forgetting root data to the ordinary Picard groupoid, the square from I//H through E and D↦O_X(−D) commutes. The separate Q-leg retains the root data; for nonempty R the retained root-sign arrows prevent a factorization of the root Picard functor through the discrete ordinary divisor groupoid. At x∉R, a_x=π_x^{-1}, a_y=1 elsewhere gives E=−[x] and Φ(a)=O_X(x)^♮ of degree [κ_x:k].
hypotheses: k is a finite field of odd characteristic; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, F=k(X), and R is a reduced finite closed subscheme, possibly empty.

proofSteps: The completed lattice of the glued line is a_xO_x, which is the completion of O_X(−E(a)). This fixes the line sign before passing to isomorphism classes.
The imported ordinary degree/divisor comparison evaluates O_X(D) as deg D; use the native weighted divisor degree, not the unweighted coefficient sum.
A right-unit arrow preserves E. A generic frame change by f adds div(f) to E; the pinned product formula makes its degree zero. Thus the degree descends to the double groupoid.
Tensor and inverse multiply and invert ideles, so their weighted valuations add and negate. Check the inverse-uniformizer at an arbitrary closed point outside R.
acceptance: The sign test uses x of any residue degree, not just a rational point.
Positive and negative signed divisors both occur; no symmetric-power effectivity hypothesis is introduced.
The grading requires no degree-one point, no chosen component representative and no norm exactness or Frobenius-trace theorem.

requests.need: Specialize the existing curve/place/divisor dictionary to smooth projective geometrically connected X/k. For every signed divisor D, identify the generic fibre of O_X(D) with F and its completed stalk at each closed x with {z∈F_x : z=0 or ord_x(z)≥−D_x}=π_x^{−D_x}O_x as a submodule of F_x, naturally in divisor addition and in multiplication by rational functions. For invertible sheaves with given generic frames, a rational scalar extends to a sheaf map exactly when it carries each completed lattice into the target lattice; the extension is unique. These comparisons must commute with tensor product, duality and the already planned point/place and completed residue-field identifications. This is an exact interface to existing AlgebraicCurves Layer 12D and JacobianChallenge A, not a request to rebuild formal patching, Picard schemes or Riemann–Roch.
